questions.problem:
Find ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to {(\pi /2)}^{+}}f(x)$ for the function given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sec}⁡x & \text{ for }\,-\frac{\pi }{2}<x<0 \\ \operatorname{cot}⁡x+x & \text{ for }\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le x<\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Approaching $x=0$ from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=2\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}2\operatorname{sec}⁡x \\  & =2\operatorname{sec}⁡0 \\  & =2(1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ from the right, we have $x>\frac{\pi }{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡x+x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(\pi /2)}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(\pi /2)}^{+}}(\operatorname{cot}⁡x+x) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =0+\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
For the piecewise function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x-1\, & \text{ for }\,x<2 \\ {x}^{2}+bx+3\, & \text{ for }\,x>2\end{aligned}
$$

it is known that ${lim}_{x\to 2}f(x)$ exists. What is the value of the constant $b?$
questions.worked_solution:
In order for ${lim}_{x\to 2}f(x)$ to exist, the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal.

- Approaching from the left, we have $x<2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}+x-1.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}{x}^{2}+x-1 \\  & =(2)^{2}+2-1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}+bx+3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}{x}^{2}+bx+3 \\  & =(2)^{2}+b\cdot 2+3 \\  & =7+2b.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) \\ 5 & =7+2b \\ 2b & =-2 \\ b & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{2x+5}-\sqrt{2x}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}(\sqrt{2x+5}-\sqrt{2x}) \\  & =\sqrt{(2\cdot 2)+5}-\sqrt{2\cdot 2} \\  & =\sqrt{9}-\sqrt{4} \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
